Not only are the Liberal Government stripping millions from an already stretched education department, Eric Abetz has flagged plans to cut workers compensation entitlements. 
 
Instead of making life harder for injured workers, let's make workplaces safer.

Cut injuries. Not protections.

Tasmania needs skilled workers.

So naturally, the Liberal Government is cutting TAFE 🙃 🤡

Emergency departments bursting at the seams.

Cuts have real life consequences for Tasmanians.

#stopthecuts
With services already buckling, and people waiting years for test results, the Liberal Government cannot be serious about cutting more funding from our health system #stopthecuts

Teachers deserve a safe workplace, just like any other worker.

They also deserve a government and leadership that doesn’t brush off an increase in assaults and violence as a result of an encouragement to report.

As the Australian Education Union Tasmania points out, violence in our schools is being driven by socio-economic complexity and school resourcing failing to keep pace with student demand. 

We need action to keep school staff safe alongside a government willing to tackle the underlying issues facing students at home.

Unions Tasmania would like to extend our deepest condolences and solidarity to the Cocker family on the passing of Simon. 

Simon was a dedicated trade unionist and led Unions Tasmania as Secretary between 2004 and 2017. Prior to this, he was the Regional Secretary of the CPSU - Community and Public Sector Union's Tasmanian branch. 

Simon led Unions Tasmania during the successful Your Rights at Work campaign against John Howard's WorkChoices laws. The national union movement mounted one of its fiercest campaigns in history. Labor won all five Tasmanian federal seats as the country rejected the Liberal Party's attack on worker's pay and conditions. 

Simon was a passionate workplace safety advocate and worked tirelessly for action on safe asbestos removal from workplaces and the broader community. 

You would also see Simon as an enthusiastic member of the The Tasmanian Grassroots Union Choir, sharing his passion for working class story telling through music.

He will be deeply missed. Vale, Simon Cocker.
